conbody.p:
Abstract: This section covers the Paragraph style in HTML — its role as the primary carrier of explanatory, introductory, and transitional prose in any technical document — and four scenarios: a paragraph in a concept topic, a paragraph containing mixed inline character styles, a paragraph placed before the first heading, and a code paragraph. The converter maps each paragraph to a

element inside the classified topic body, extracts the based on the paragraph context, and maps recognized inline character styles to their corresponding DITA inline elements.
Paragraphsare the fundamental unit of prose communication in any technical publication. They carry three types of content as described below:

ul.li: Explanatory content that defines concepts and terms.
Introductory content that sets the context for the structured elements that follow such as list, workflows, tables, procedures, and images.
Transitional content that connects sections and chapters through the document's logic.

conbody.p: This prose content is essential not only for readability but for building complete technical context, search discoverability and structural completeness.
conbody.note: A topic consisting only of a list or a table, with no surrounding prose, is a valid but an incomplete piece of technical communication. It is recommended to add the context to such structured elements.
conbody.p: In well-structured HTML, introductory paragraphs establish the context for a topic before lists, tables, or images present supporting information. Inline elements such as <strong>, <em>, <code>, and other recognized HTML tags provide semantic emphasis within the surrounding paragraph without changing its structural role.

conbody.note:
Paragraphs should always appear within a heading-delimited section. A

element placed before the first heading is treated as pre-heading content and is processed according to a separate conversion rule. Use paragraphs to present meaningful content rather than visual spacing, and rely on recognized inline markup instead of manual formatting to convey emphasis.
